title: RNN Brain-to-Text Interface Decodes Attempted Handwriting from Paralysis at 90 Characters/Min
whyItMatters: Published in Nature: decodes attempted handwriting from motor-cortex neural spikes in a paralyzed participant at 90 characters/min (94.1% online / >99% LM accuracy)—more than doubling prior BCI typing records.
summary: Francis R. Willett, Donald T. Avansino, Leigh R. Hochberg, Jaimie M. Henderson, and Krishna V. Shenoy (Stanford University, HHMI, and BrainGate) demonstrated in Nature an intracortical brain-computer interface that uses a recurrent neural network decoder to translate imagined handwriting movements directly from motor-cortex spiking activity into real-time text. A clinical trial participant paralyzed from the neck down achieved 90 characters per minute with 94.1% raw online accuracy—and >99% accuracy with a language model—more than doubling prior point-and-click BCI speeds and approaching able-bodied smartphone typing (115 chars/min).
technicalHighlights: RNN neural decoder translated attempted handwriting trajectories from motor-cortex microelectrode arrays into real-time text at 90 characters per minute.
Achieved 94.1% raw online accuracy and >99% accuracy with a general-purpose autocorrect language model in a participant with spinal cord injury.
Proved that temporally rich dexterous movements are far easier to separate in neural state space than point-to-point cursor motions, launching modern speech BCIs.
caveats: Demonstrated in a single clinical-trial participant using surgically implanted Utah microelectrode arrays; indexed as a 2021 historical calibration anchor.

scoreRationale.foundational: Pioneered RNN sequence decoding of complex dexterous motor intent, breaking the cursor-typing ceiling for paralyzed communication.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly enabled Stanford’s 62-WPM speech neuroprosthesis (2023), UC Davis’s 97.5% speech BCI (2024), and modern clinical neuroprosthetics.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature (May 2021) with live human clinical trial demonstration and public neural dataset release.
scoreRationale.velocity: More than doubled decades-old BCI typing speeds in a single architectural leap to sequence-based RNN decoding.
